comment: Agent NDA signatures, acceptance, acts, states and the bound test, with real Ed25519 signatures (agentnda.net 0.1.2-draft, 6, 6.1, 7.1, 7.3, 8.1). The documents are the specification's example (Harbor & Line Outfitters' open offer and Caldera Freight Systems' acceptance, byte for byte as nda-offer.json pins them) and agreements built from it. Every signature is real: the keys are derived from the published seeds below, and Ed25519 is deterministic, so any implementation reproduces each sig byte for byte. The test seeds are public by design and sign nothing else. A sig is the padded base64 of the 64-byte signature. Every expected answer is written from the specification, not computed by an implementation. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: change it only with a spec change alongside.
spec: Agent NDA 0.1.2-draft: 6 (signatures), 6.1 (acceptance), 6.2 (mandates), 7.1 (states), 7.3 (acts), 8 (references), 8.1 (whether a party is bound); Agent RFP 0.9.1-draft 5.11.3 checks 1 to 5

keys.comment: Each seed is the SHA-256 of its label, as UTF-8. seed_hex is the raw 32-byte Ed25519 seed and public the public key in the family's spelling. The seeds are given as hex only, so that no secret-shaped string sits in the fixture. The agent keys of Harbor & Line and Caldera Freight are the stand-ins the specification prints and have no seed; they never sign, because owners sign.

signatures.comment: 6: every signature record verifies over the signed bytes, except the discloser's on an acceptance, marked over: offer, which verifies over the offer bytes. A signature is checked against the key its record names.

cases.why: the recipient signs the completed document
the offer bytes re-derived from a changed document are not the bytes the discloser signed

acceptance.comment: 6.1: the five checks a verifier runs on an acceptance, in order; the first that fails is reported. resolve maps a handle to the agent key it currently names, for step 4.

cases.why: any change beyond parties.recipient and disclosure.recipient breaks the discloser's signature
the offer was withdrawn on 2026-10-21, and Caldera signed on 2026-10-22
a withdrawal leaves acceptances made before it standing

act_checks.comment: 7.3: an act verifies under its own tag over its own body, names the agreement by id, version and digest (the offer digest for a withdrawn offer, the completed agreement's digest otherwise, since acceptances of one offer share an identifier), is signed by a key that signed the agreement, and carries a mandate where the acting seat names an organization (6.2). act_bytes pins the signed bytes of one act.

cases.why: an act on one acceptance carries that acceptance's digest
the key signed no seat of the agreement
Harbor & Line's seat names an organization, so its acts carry a mandate

states.comment: 7.1: the state derived from signatures, acts and instants at now. effective_at is when the duties began (effective_at, or the last required signature), ended_at when the agreement stopped covering new disclosures, duties_end_at that plus the survival period (5.2), counted in days of 86,400 seconds.

cases.why: notice_days 30 from 2027-03-01T12:00:00Z; survival 730 days from then
a renderer MUST NOT show one signature as in force
the agreement stays in force among the others while at least two remain; after the third member left on 2027-04-01 one remained, and one member alone is no agreement

bound.comment: 8.1: is this party bound by the named agreement at now? rule 1, it signed a seat; rule 2, the reference is an open offer and it is the recipient of an acceptance that passes 6.1; rule 3, it is the subcontractor of a flow-down agreement that passes the strictness test of 5.5 and names an agreement binding the party above it. The agreement must be in force. documents lists what the caller holds.

gate.comment: Agent RFP 0.9.1-draft 5.11.3, checks 1 to 5: what a board checks about the agreement before it releases a gated body. Check 6, that the posting is open and addresses the provider, is the board's own. The gate names the offer by its offer digest. poster is the posting's poster.agent; requester is the agent key on the request's transport identity.
